title: Man. Post. Cap. IV: Rursus observata — spiraculum / lignum / mors; before triple life
pass_a_gloss: CHAPTER IV. Again certain things observed and reprehended in the same Cap. II. I noted certain things, Reverend and most beloved Brother in Christ, in the second Chapter of Your treatise. Suffer me also to refute certain things. For you say certain things concerning the breath of life, concerning the tree of life, and concerning the death threatened to Adam, which I neither approve, nor do I sufficiently grasp what moment they contribute to that which you undertook to prove in that chapter; but once refuted they can help my cause.
pass_b_english: Chapter IV. Further observations and censures on the same chapter II.

I marked several points, Reverend and most beloved Brother in Christ, in the second chapter of your treatise. Allow me to answer some of them as well. You say things about the breath of life, the tree of life, and the death threatened to Adam. I neither approve those claims, nor see what they do for the thesis you set out to prove in that chapter—but once answered, they can help my case.
source_text: CAPUT IV. Rursus quaedam observata & reprehensa in eodem Cap. II. Notavi quaedam, Reverende & dilectissime in Christo Frater, in secundo Capite Tui tractatus. Patere me etiam quaedam refellere. Dicis enim quaedam de spiraculo vitae, de ligno vitae, deque morte interminata Adamo, quae, nec probo, nec quid momenti ad id conferant, quod tu eo capite probare instituisti, satis assequor, refutata autem meam causam juvare possunt.

choices.choice: Mark three Cap. II loci to refute: breath, tree, threatened death
